items.title: Man Convicted of Leaving Hairstylist's Body in Alley, Disposing Evidence
items.summary:
A man has been found guilty of leaving a Colorado woman’s body in an alley for nearly two months and disposing of her belongings in an attempt to conceal her death.

Brandon David Mumma was convicted of tampering with a deceased human body and tampering with evidence on Thursday, November 19, in connection with his actions following Jax Gratton’s death, according to Colorado’s First Judicial District Attorney’s Office .

Mumma, 44, is believed to be the last person who was with Gratton before she went missing. She was later discovered dead in an alley in between two buildings, one of which housed Mumma’s office in Lakewood, on July 6, 2025, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors accused Mumma of tossing her body out of his office window after she died of a drug overdose on April 16, 2025, according to The Denver Post , which reports Gratton, 34, had worked as a hairstylist in Denver.

Man Indicted in Connection With Death of Colorado Hairstylist Jax Gratton 

“Jax’s loved ones have endured the anguish of searching for her, the devastation of losing her, and the pain of unanswered questions about her death,” First Judicial Circuit District Attorney Alexis King said in a statement included in a Thursday news release. “Today’s verdicts hold Mr. Mumma accountable for his actions after her death and his efforts to conceal what happened.”

Mumma and Gratton were in a “consensual intimate relationship” ahead of her death, prosecutors said in a March news release announcing his indictment in the case.

Brandon Mumma Summit County Sheriff’s Office

“My whole entire ❤️,” Abby McKivitz posted via her Instagram Story on Monday, November 23, sharing the 49ers’ message of support for Colton.  

Colton suffered the injury on Sunday, November 22, when his leg was rolled up during the second quarter of the game in Mexico City. He was placed in an air cast before being taken off the field via a cart.  

After the game, 49ers head coach, Kyle Shanahan , said the team believed Colton’s ankle was “broken and dislocated.” San Francisco has yet to release an official statement about Colton’s injury, but it is widely presumed he will miss the rest of the season.  

49ers’ Colton McKivitz Shows Aftermath of Gnarly Ankle Injury in Vikings Game 

“That was really crushing,” Shanahan, 46, said on Sunday. “Colton has had an unbelievable year. … It was tough to see Colton go down like that.” 

Colton and Abby got married in June 2025 at The Clubhouse at Talons in Ankeny, Iowa, Abby’s home state.  

“Forever & a day 🤍,” Abby posted via Instagram at the time.

items.title: Florida Politician Insists Son Was Murdered: ‘Not a Freak Hunting Accident’
items.summary:
Two days after a 19-year-old was fatally shot while camping, his politician father is insisting his son’s death “was not a freak hunting accident” but the result of “malicious intent.”

Escambia County District 4 Commissioner Joe Vinson claimed that his son, Carey Washington Vinson , was inside his tent at a sandbar campground near Blackwater River in Florida on Sunday, November 22, when a bullet fired from outside of the campsite struck his son.

Chief Deputy Randy Tifft of the Santa Rosa County Sheriff’s Office previously said that Carey, 19, and his friends had been camping in different areas and sandbars since Friday, November 20, according to People . When Carey was shot in the head at 11:30 p.m., a vehicle was reportedly parked on the other side of the river.

Carey’s friends claimed to authorities that they heard the vehicle turn on and start driving after the shots were fired. The friends also said they yelled in the direction of the vehicle to make it known that they were in the area.

BF Killed 16-Year-Old, Then 'Callously Dumped' Body After 'Toxic' Relationship 

Tifft added that no one should have been hunting in the area because it was so late at night.

On Tuesday, November 24, Vinson — who was sworn in as the first non-party-affiliated District 4 commissioner in Escambia County’s history on November 17 — issued a statement about the tragedy, saying he needed to “correct a misimpression” that the shooting was an accident.

“This was not a freak hunting accident — not someone firing carelessly in the dark,” he said in the statement posted via social media.…

items.title: Biggest Revelations From Derek Hough and Wife Hayley's Documentary
items.summary:
Derek Hough and wife Hayley Erbert are pulling back the curtain on their relationship — and her near fatal brain bleed — in the new documentary The Symphony of Dance. 

The film followed the couple on the final leg of their tour in 2023, when Erbert, 32, experienced a medical emergency.

“At the very beginning of the opening number, there’s a move where she kind of comes down to my arms, I wrap her up and she twists really fast. We both move our head[s] forward and we hit heads very hard. We both kind of [were] looking at each other like, ‘Are you OK?’” Hough, 41, recalled.

Erbert added, “I probably had five dances left, and all of a sudden, I get this excruciating headache, just on the right side. I didn’t know exactly what to do in that moment except for [think], ‘OK, just go back out on stage and just keep pushing through. You’re almost done with the show.’ Derek says I didn’t skip a beat, I didn’t miss a step. I actually don’t remember any of it. And then I came off stage and collapsed.”

Hough recalled Erbert “dying” on the ground, having seizures. She eventually underwent an emergency craniectomy for a hematoma . Weeks later, Erbert had a second surgery to replace a large portion of her skull that was removed in the initial procedure.

Erbert ultimately returned to the stage just months later. The pair went on to welcome their daughter , Everley, in 2025. The film is dedicated to their daughter.

items.title: Woman Pretended Child Died to Befriend Elderly Woman, Defrauded Her of $85K
items.summary:
A Vermont woman will serve prison time for defrauding an elderly woman she befriended and manipulated in a scheme to steal thousands of dollars from her, federal prosecutors said.

Chief U.S. District Judge Christina Reiss sentenced Jessica Russell , of Williamstown, to one year and eight months in prison on Friday, November 20, after she pleaded guilty to two federal counts of wire fraud, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont said in a news release.

The judge also ordered Russell, 43, to pay nearly $85,000 in restitution to the victim’s family and imposed a $75,945.16 forfeiture money judgment, according to prosecutors.

The restitution figure, $84,420.16, reflects the amount of money Russell stole from the woman to buy herself a home and a car, prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memorandum obtained by Us .

Woman Accused of Spending Her Mom's 'Life Savings,' Locking Her in Bedroom 

Russell’s federal public defender, Sara M. Puls , didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us .

Authorities discovered Russell financially took advantage of the woman, who has dementia, after firefighters found the woman “confused and injured, trapped in a filthy residence in Barton, Vermont” during extensive flooding in 2023, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said in its release.

Russell later admitted as part of her plea agreement that she befriended the woman between the summer of 2013 and July 2023, partly by pretending her child had died, as the woman had experienced the death of her own child, according to prosecutors.

“I don’t want to sit here and be like, ‘Boo-hoo-hoo me’ all the time about this whole thing because now it’s about kind of getting boots on the ground now and getting myself together,” Applegate, 54, said during the Tuesday, November 24, episode of her and Jamie Lynn Sigler ’s “MeSsy” podcast. “It really does feel good to feel understood because it’s a hard thing to come out and say that I’m upset that I don’t have MS, right?”

Addressing her critics, the Dead to Me alum continued, “A lot of people had a lot to f***ing say about it after I came out. But, you know, it’s not about that. It’s about an identity thing. … It’s about a community that I love still, as we know.”

Applegate also pointed out that having a diagnosis allowed her to “relax” into her illness rather than constantly searching for answers about what’s wrong with her health.

Why Christina Applegate Is Not ‘Happy’ About No Longer Having MS

Applegate first announced her battle with what she believed to be MS in 2021. After five years of detailing her health journey and advocating for MS patients, the actress revealed in October that she had been misdiagnosed with the autoimmune disorder.

items.title: Former Teacher Arrested for Holding Baby After Sexting Underage Student
items.summary:
A former teacher in Kentucky was arrested for a second time after she allegedly violated her bond conditions by holding a newborn baby.

Rachel Clement ’s bond was revoked on Monday, November 23, after prosecutors learned of the incident. Clement was arrested for a second time after she held the 2-week-old child when she went to a church that is attached to a school on November 13 to drop off birthday party decorations.

Clement previously pleaded guilty to two counts of sexual abuse and one count of evidence tampering in October after she was caught having a sexual relationship with a student at Henderson High School in Henderson, Kentucky, according to The Hendersonian .

As part of her plea deal, Clement, 29, registered as a sex offender, was barred from school premises and was prohibited from having contact with minors except for her biological niece, according to the outlet.

1st Grade Teacher in Tennessee Charged With Abuse of Her Own 2 Kids 

Following her second arrest, Clement’s attorney, Jonathan Coomes , argued that his client was at the church at the pastor’s request. He also told the outlet that she had no contact with school-age children and that she left the premises before students arrived.

Coomes went on to argue that the child that Clement held was “not similar in characteristics to the victim in the present case,” noting that her victim was a teenager. It is not currently clear if Clement had a relation to the child in question.

Clement is facing up to three years in prison on each sexual abuse charge and five years for evidence tampering. She is…
